requirements.evidence: Every part of the contract is in the diff. The migrations add the named indexes and the stored generated owner_seq column (create_entity_memberships_table.php:21-28). Models, the enum with manageable(), the factories with states, both policies, the entity.pick controller with Gate::authorize('view') and the audit log line (EntityPickController.php:18-26), and the routes under auth+verified (routes/web.php:30-35) are all present. All three Livewire pages authorize in mount(). Members covers the duplicate error on email (AddMember.php:29-31), owner role rejected on role (Members.php:54-56) and the last-manager 403 (RemoveMember.php:24-32). Settings has a locked entity, a slug unique rule ignoring itself, delete clearing the session, and an atomic transfer that checks for an admin other than the caller and a vanished owner (TransferOwnership.php:27-37). Lang keys exist in both locales and docs/database-schema.md is updated.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through new app/Actions/* classes that authorize inside (AddMember, AssignRole, RemoveMember, DeleteEntity, UpdateEntity, TransferOwnership). Models use #[Fillable]. The nav is extracted into an anonymous Blade component (components/entity-nav.blade.php). Pages use Bulma markup. CHANGELOG, business-rules.md and database-schema.md are updated. Deviations: Settings mixes #[Validate] for name with a rules() method for slug (Settings.php:22, 83-95). assignRole validates the role with Validator::make instead of the #[Validate] pattern (Members.php:54). targetMembershipId has no validation attribute.

security.evidence: Every public action calls $this->authorize and the Action authorizes again. Client IDs are resolved and scoped to the locked entity (Members.php:91-99 membershipOf). The entity is #[Locked] in all three components. TransferOwnership looks the target up through $entity->memberships() with lockForUpdate. Output uses {{ }} everywhere. Smaller gaps: targetMembershipId is unvalidated, though it is safely resolved and scoped. The RemoveMember last-manager count is not done under a lock, so it is racy (RemoveMember.php:24-32). DeleteEntity authorizes 'delete', which admins pass (EntityPolicy.php:40), so the owner-only rule depends on the component check.

tests.evidence: There are thorough Pest tests: DataModelTest covers the unique indexes, second owner rejected and cascades. PolicyTest uses datasets per role. MembersTest has a tamper test for a membership id from another entity, employee 403s, the owner role rejected and the last-manager case. SettingsTest covers a locked-entity swap that throws CannotUpdateLockedPropertyException, an admin calling save directly getting 403, transfer to employee/self/foreign/missing all getting 403, the vanished owner and the blank placeholder. PickEntityTest covers the audit log and the session left untouched on 403. DashboardTest asserts the settings URL is absent for non-owners. One weak spot: the vanished-owner test is stopped by the component's manageSettings check before the action's own owner-null branch runs.

simplicity.evidence: The code is mostly lean and reuses existing x-form-field/x-button components. Authorization runs twice, once in each component method and again in each Action (e.g. Members.php:40 and AddMember.php:22). That is defence in depth, but redundant. The @can checks on each table row call membershipFor once per row, which is an N+1 query (members.blade.php:33,47).

readability.evidence: Methods are small and well named, with PHPDoc on the public action methods. There are useful comments, such as 'Demote first: the (entity_id, owner_seq) unique index allows one owner at a time.' (TransferOwnership.php:34). UserRole::isManager() makes the role checks clear. There is no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task. There is no onboarding, entity switcher, middleware or navbar redesign. The only doc removals (owner_membership_id, locale_default) bring the schema doc in line with what was implemented.

issues.explanation: The last-manager count and the delete are not in a locked transaction. Two managers removing each other at the same time could leave the entity with no owner or admin.
DeleteEntity authorizes the 'delete' ability, which admins pass. Owner-only deletion is enforced only by the Settings component, not inside the Action that does the write.
Validation styles are mixed: name uses #[Validate], slug uses rules(), and the public targetMembershipId has no validation at all. The project's pattern is #[Validate] on every public input property.
The role argument is checked with Validator::make in the component and checked again inside AssignRole (AssignRole.php:23-25), so the same rule is enforced twice.
The @can checks on each row run a membershipFor query per row, which is an N+1 pattern on the members list.
After the owner row is deleted the component's manageSettings check fails first, so the action's own owner-null branch is never exercised.

review.summary: The change builds the full entity data model: migrations with a portable one-owner constraint, models, the enum, factories and policies. It adds the pick controller and the Dashboard, Members and Settings Livewire pages, with authorized Action classes, both lang files, docs and a strong Pest suite that includes tamper and unauthorized-call tests. Only minor issues remain: a racy last-manager check, owner-only deletion enforced only in the component, and inconsistent validation on Settings properties. I would approve with nits.
